prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1481; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to what happened, but I'll say my name is on file already. Go ahead.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving and what the weather and road conditions were like?
A: I was heading down the main road in League City, going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. It was clear, dry pavement, nothing unusual.
Q: Walk me through the collision itself.
A: A car came over into my lane while it was passing a truck. I tried to swerve but there wasn't much room. We hit head-on, but it was a slow impact, not like a highway crash. Both of our cars stopped pretty quickly.
Q: Did either vehicle's airbags deploy?
A: Mine did. The other car's I'm not sure about. The steering wheel and the airbag hit me hard enough that I felt it in my chest and shoulder.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle right away? Were you able to move?
A: I got out on my own, but my left shoulder was throbbing and I couldn't lift my arm very well. I sat on the curb until the ambulance came.
Q: Did you receive medical treatment at the scene or afterward?
A: They took me by ambulance to the emergency room. They did X-rays and gave me a sling and some pain medication. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week since then.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries or problems with that same shoulder?
A: Nothing serious. I had some soreness years ago from lifting, but it went away and I didn't need treatment.
Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limited movement?
A: Yes. Lifting anything over my head is hard, and it aches when I sleep on that side. My doctor says it could take a few more months to get back to normal.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was driving carefully and I didn't do anything to cause this. I'd like to get it resolved so I can get back to work.
Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the recorded statement.
